name: Cefoperazone

overview.mechanism: A beta-lactam antibacterial that inhibits bacterial cell-wall synthesis.
uses: Susceptible bacterial infections; cefoperazone alone is distinct from cefoperazone/sulbactam combinations.

paragraphs.text: Historical pharmacokinetic studies describe substantial biliary elimination and relatively small half-life changes with isolated renal failure. Biliary obstruction can prolong elimination and shift a larger fraction of drug clearance to the kidneys.

Consequently, low usual urinary recovery should not be converted into a blanket statement of safety in combined hepatic and renal dysfunction. This single-agent evidence does not define sulbactam dosing in combination products.

evidence.title: US label: renal failure, hepatic disease and bleeding

paragraphs.text: The 2024 US CEFOBID IV/IM label states that usual doses need no adjustment in isolated renal failure, but recommends periodic serum drug concentrations with high doses and reduction if accumulation occurs. In combined hepatic dysfunction and significant renal disease, it limits dosing to 1–2 g/day unless serum concentrations are closely monitored. It schedules dosing after hemodialysis. These statements concern cefoperazone alone, not cefoperazone/sulbactam.

The label warns of serious, sometimes fatal hemorrhage and calls for monitoring for bleeding, thrombocytopenia and coagulopathy. Vitamin K deficiency can occur; prothrombin time should be monitored in at-risk patients, including those with poor nutrition or malabsorption. The product contains 34 mg sodium (1.5 mEq) per gram. A disulfiram-like reaction has been reported with alcohol within 72 hours after administration.

sources.citation: A review and summary of the pharmacokinetics of cefoperazone: a new, extended-spectrum beta-lactam antibiotic. PubMed PMID: 6455787.
